ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a benzene ring structure. The right side of the benzene ring is connected through a single bond to a nitrogen atom; this nitrogen atom is further connected to another nitrogen atom in the form of a triple bond, forming a benzenediazonium structure. The figure also shows positive and negative charge labels, curved arrows, and an OH/hydroxide part on the right. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and method requirements, ignore curved arrows and charges, and do not count any bonds involving hydrogen. The benzene ring itself has 6 C–C bonds; there is 1 C–N bond between the benzene ring and nitrogen; the N≡N between the two nitrogens is counted as 1 bond; the O–H bond in OH involves hydrogen and is not counted. Therefore the total is 6 + 1 + 1 = 8.

method.method_draft: Ignore the curved arrows and charges. Count the non-hydrogen bonds in the benzene-diazonium structure component by component: the benzene ring has 6 C–C bonds around the ring; the ring carbon is connected to nitrogen by 1 C–N bond; the two nitrogens are connected by 1 N≡N bond. Do not count the O–H bond in the hydroxide/HO part because it involves hydrogen. Total = 6 + 1 + 1 = 8.

method.method_draft: Construct the non-hydrogen connectivity graph. The phenyl ring is a 6-member carbon cycle, so it contributes 6 heavy-atom edges. The substituent adds one edge from the ring carbon to the first N and one edge from that N to the terminal N. The OH species contributes no counted edge because its only drawn bond is O–H, which is excluded. Therefore the heavy-atom edge count is 6 + 2 + 0 = 8.

推理：按非氢原子的连通关系计数。苯环是六元碳环，提供 6 条碳-碳重原子连接。苯环与第一个氮之间有 1 条重原子连接，第一个氮与末端氮之间有 1 条重原子连接。OH 物种中可见的键是 O-H，涉及氢，因此不计入。总数为 6 + 2 + 0 = 8。
